ideas.title: Push off in the hull you chose
ideas.critique: This is round 1's three hulls, now with the player's choice and Lumi's body in it. That removes the risk that it is just objects moving alone in front of a fixed camera, and Lumi's weight tipping a tender hull is a payoff anyone can read. The weak points are that the player chooses from three ready-made hulls instead of making one, which is a long way from 'keeps what I did to it', and that pushing and climbing with Lumi's body is the animation most likely to slide and pop.

ideas.title: A weir of stones you set
ideas.nearest: Skipping stones, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is round 1's stream idea at a patch size that can actually run live. Water that banks up, jets and fills a pond the player built, checked against Ritter, is real and something people come back to. Placing stones is stacking more than making, so the big goal only moves a little, and a stone footprint baked into the heightfield will look like a raised block if the carrying and setting are not animated well.

ideas.title: Lay a campfire that catches
ideas.critique: Heat moving stick to stick, with thickness, moisture and packing deciding whether a fire catches, is a new kind of material behaviour, and a fire that dies when it is laid badly is a lesson in play. 'Things that burn' is also named in the human's goals, and an emissive glow lighting the ground repeats the hot-glass still. The combustion here is a lumped per-stick model, so if the flames are a shader over temperature numbers it will read as sticks changing colour.

ideas.title: Bore a flute from a reed
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Tone holes as side branches on a transmission line is real woodwind acoustics, and a hole that cannot be made smaller is exactly the 'keeps what I did' rule. It is still a third 'shape it and hear its solved note' film after the stone and the lantern. The jet excitation is the part that usually sounds synthetic, and a film of holes being bored shows almost nothing to someone watching with the sound off.
